                    ### Question
                    A 38-year-old man presents with pruritus and jaundice. Past medical history is significant for ulcerative colitis diagnosed 2 years ago, well managed medically. He is vaccinated against hepatitis A and B and denies any recent travel abroad. On physical examination, prominent hepatosplenomegaly is noted. Which of the following would confirm the most likely diagnosis in this patient?

opb. Contrast CT of the abdomen

opd. Percutaneous liver biopsy
ope. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP)

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient, a 38-year-old man with pruritus, jaundice, and hepatosplenomegaly, has a history of ulcerative colitis, which is a known risk factor for primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). ERCP is considered the gold standard for diagnosing PSC as it allows for direct visualization of the bile ducts and can identify strictures characteristic of the disease. While MRCP is non-invasive and can suggest bile duct abnormalities, ERCP provides definitive diagnosis and potential therapeutic intervention. Therefore, the most likely diagnosis in this patient is PSC, and the best confirmatory test is ERCP.
